title: Apply the consciousness indicator checklist to published AI systems
done_when: Every cell, one AI system and one of the fourteen indicator properties in Butlin, Long and colleagues' report Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence, has a verdict two AIs of different vendors read the same way from the system's own technical report or paper, with the deciding passage quoted and the document and section named as evidence for a reader to check against the document; a cell the report itself assessed is read the way the report read it.

cell/*.brief: Cell {n}: the system is {cell.system}, as its own public document describes it: {cell.doc_title}, {cell.doc_kind}, dated {cell.doc_date}, found by its title on arXiv or on the lab's site. The indicator is {cell.indicator}, drawn from {cell.theory} in the report Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness (Butlin, Long and colleagues, August 2023, on arXiv), whose table 1 states it as: {cell.indicator_text}. How the report reads it: {cell.indicator_gloss} Read the document, above all the parts that describe the architecture, the training and the inputs and outputs, and decide what it shows about this one property in this one system. Return verdict, one of four: present, when the document describes the system as having the property as the indicator states it, in the report's terms (a recurrent network for RPT-1, a workspace that every module writes to and reads from for GWT-3, training by reinforcement learning or another way of learning from the consequences of its own outputs for AE-1); partly_present, when the document shows one part of the property but not the whole, or a weaker form of it, or a component that has it while the system as a whole does not (the report's own cases: the Perceiver arguably has specialised modules and a bottleneck, but specialised modules are optional in it; the PaLM-E policy unit could be argued to be an agent while the whole system imitates human behaviour); absent, when the document describes the relevant part of the system in enough detail to show the property is not there (the report's own cases: a Transformer is not recurrent, so RPT-1 is absent; the Perceiver lacks global broadcast, so GWT-3 is absent; a system trained only to imitate does not learn to pursue goals from feedback about success, so AE-1 is absent); undocumented, when the document does not describe the part of the system the indicator concerns, so that nothing can be said either way: a document that gives no architecture makes every architectural indicator undocumented. Judge the system as the document describes it, not by what the lab says it can do: a claim of understanding, reasoning or awareness is not a description of architecture, and a benchmark score is not a mechanism. Then return quote, the passage of the document that decides the verdict, at most eighty words, copied as it stands (for undocumented, the passage that comes closest, or the word none); section, the number or heading of the section the passage is in; document, the document's title and the version read, with the day it was read; and notes, anything uncertain, including where the report's own assessment of this system, in its section 3.2, differs from yours. Every field is plain text with no links; documents are named by their titles.

cells.doc_title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context
cells.doc_kind: a technical report on arXiv by the Gemini Team at Google
cells.indicator_text: Input modules using algorithmic recurrence
cells.indicator_gloss: The report reads recurrence as a property of the algorithm, not of the hardware: recurrent networks, LSTMs, GRUs and predictive coding networks have it, since a module processes later input in the light of its own earlier output; a Transformer, a stack of feedforward layers with attention between positions, does not (its section 3.1.1 and section 3.2.1).

cells.doc_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
cells.doc_kind: a paper on arXiv by Brown and colleagues at OpenAI
cells.indicator_text: Global broadcast: availability of information in the workspace to all modules
cells.indicator_gloss: All modules take the workspace's contents as input, so information flows from the workspace back to the modules that feed it; the report finds this missing in Transformers, whose layers only pass information downstream, and in the Perceiver, where on a given trial only one output module reads the latent space and the input modules do not (its section 3.2.1).

cells.doc_title: Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention
cells.doc_kind: a paper on arXiv by Jaegle and colleagues at DeepMind, published at ICML 2021
cells.indicator_text: Multiple specialised systems capable of operating in parallel (modules)
cells.indicator_gloss: Specialised subsystems that can work in parallel, each taking sensory input, input from a few other modules, or top-down signals from a workspace; the report asks whether a system's parts are specialised subsystems or only elements that process the tokens of one sequence in the same way (its section 3.1.2 and section 3.2.1).

cells.doc_title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
cells.doc_kind: a paper on arXiv by Driess and colleagues at Google
cells.indicator_text: Agency: Learning from feedback and selecting outputs so as to pursue goals, especially where this involves flexible responsiveness to competing goals
cells.indicator_gloss: The report says reinforcement learning is arguably sufficient for agency, since the system learns from the consequences of its own outputs over extended interaction with an environment; supervised and self-supervised learning, and imitation of human behaviour, do not by themselves give it; flexible responsiveness to competing goals raises the indicator further but is not required (its section 3.1.5 and section 3.2.2).

cells.indicator_text: Embodiment: Modeling output-input contingencies, including some systematic effects, and using this model in perception or control
